messages:
Anya: Heads-up — ran into a nasty split-brain when we moved admission heuristics into the adapter. Two batchers raced to accept the same tenant and both started draining KV warmups.
Theo: Oof. Do you have a repro?
Anya: Minimal repro: 2 adapters, same tenant, tight deadline hint, prefetch + admission in adapter. Race on enqueue -> both return ACCEPT and backlog_hint=0.
Rohit: That matches some failure traces I saw from the e2e tests. Adapters don't coordinate on slot grants.
Marta: Can we surface a stronger contract from adapter -> scheduler? Right now adapter returns boolean + hint, but it's insufficient for handoff.
Anya: Agreed. Current primitive: ACCEPT/REJECT + backlog_hint. We need deterministic tie-break or a lease token.
Sam: Proposal: EnqueueResponse {decision: enum, lease_id?: string, lease_ttl_ms?: int, backlog_hint: int, deadline_ms?: int} so only holder of lease can kick off warmup/evict.
Theo: I like lease. But how do we avoid extra RPC latency for every enqueue? It's hot path.
Rohit: Optimize: adapters only request lease when backlog_hint < threshold OR deadline tight. Normal enqueues use lightweight fastpath (optimistic ACCEPT) with transient soft-lease.
Anya: Sketch of fastpath:
```
// pseudo
if (backlog_hint > HOT_THRESHOLD) return ACCEPT_FAST;
else return REQUEST_LEASE(async)
```
If two adapters both ACCEPT_FAST, scheduler must have an idempotent drain step to detect double-warmup.
Marta: So add a drain registration: adapter calls RegisterDrain(lease_id) before heavy work. Scheduler dedups by tenant+epoch and returns ALREADY_REGISTERED if someone else is doing work.
Sam: That shifts complexity to scheduler but keeps enqueue low-latency. Worth it. Need idempotent register + cancel paths.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher v2.3 queued: rolling deploy to test-cluster in 10m.
Theo: Concern: RegisterDrain itself might become hot. Use per-tenant sharded registry keyed by tenant hash, keep it in-memory on leader for shard. If leader fails, lease TTL expires.
Rohit: TTL semantics must tie to K/V warmup progress. Maybe warmup heartbeats extend lease_ttl. If warmup stalls, scheduler can preempt after N missed heartbeats.
Anya: Also need clear metrics: "register_conflicts", "fastpath_double_accepts", "lease_preemptions", "heartbeat_misses" — we should gate rollout on those.
Marta: API surface suggestion (minimal):
```
RegisterDrain(tenant_id, host_epoch, desired_slots) -> {status: OK|ALREADY|RETRY_LATER, lease_id?, ttl_ms?}
ExtendLease(lease_id) -> {ok|not_found}
CancelLease(lease_id) -> {ok}
```
Sam: For backpressure, adapter should respect RETRY_LATER and surface to clients with 503+Retry-After for soft throttling.
Theo: Also want to avoid adapter-scheduler chattiness for short bursts. Add local backoff with jitter and aggregate cluster-level retry budget.
Rohit: Edge-case: node crash after RegisterDrain but before warmup starts. Lease TTL ensures another adapter can take over. But we must ensure warmup work is idempotent (KV load may be expensive). Document idempotency expectations.
Anya: Action items: 1) Theo/Rohit design lease proto + shard registry. 2) Sam/Marta implement metrics and fastpath heuristics in adapter. 3) Anya run repro and create integration test for double-accept scenario.
Marta: Can we keep the adapter API backward-compatible? Add fields optional, fallback to old behavior if scheduler doesn't support register.
Sam: Yes, negotiate version via handshake on start. Graceful fallback mode: adapter uses old ACCEPT but marks op as non-optimistic (safer).
Theo: One more thought: add "deadline_hint_ms" to RegisterDrain so scheduler can prioritize preemption.
Anya: OK. I'm going to open an RFC PR with these patterns and the proto sketch. Will tag the thread. :thumbsup:
Rohit: Thanks — this should prevent cross-adapter warmup storms and simplify eviction coordination.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher v2.3 started rolling to test-cluster. Logs: https://ci.internal/release/4319991111
Sam: Ping when RFC is up, will take adapter changes.
Anya: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1234 (WIP)
